rows.verified: HSE abrasive-wheel guidance applies relevant PUWER requirements after repeal of the former Abrasive Wheels Regulations.
Abrasive-wheel work requires essential training appropriate to the equipment and operation.
Wheel characteristics and suitability must be considered before grinding operations.
Grinding-machine operations require defined safe operating procedures.
Wheel mounting procedures and mounting-related hazards require specific control.
Suitable guards are a core control for abrasive-wheel machinery.
Portable and hand-held grinders require additional precautions beyond fixed-machine controls.
Protective equipment requirements form part of safe abrasive-wheel use.
Abrasive-wheel risk depends on wheel type, machine speed, mounting, guarding, material, operator competence, maintenance and PPE.
HSE abrasive-wheel evidence is wheel-, machine-, operation-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Heat stress occurs when the body's internal temperature-control mechanisms begin to fail.
Heat-stress risk is influenced by work rate, humidity, air temperature and work clothing or PPE.
Early heat-stress signs can include poor concentration, muscle cramps, heat rash, severe thirst and fainting.
Heat exhaustion may present with fatigue, dizziness, nausea, headache and moist skin.
Heat stroke can cause confusion, convulsions and loss of consciousness and may be fatal without early detection.
Risk assessment should consider work rate, climate, clothing or PPE and individual susceptibility.
Engineering controls can include process changes, fans, air conditioning and barriers against radiant heat.
Exposure limits, cool rest breaks, drinking water, acclimatisation, training and health monitoring can reduce residual heat risk.
Heat-stress risk depends on temperature, humidity, radiant heat, work rate, clothing, hydration, acclimatisation and individual susceptibility.
HSE heat-stress evidence is workplace-, climate-, task-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
